summary: Satoru Harada is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (~1973–1976) and held positions at the Eastern Institute, Toyo Bunko, and Kokushikan University.
Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Eshō Mikogami and held posts at Ryukoku University and Osaka University of Foreign Studies.
Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University as a research student and served as a lecturer there in 2015.

Satoshi Hiraoka works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, under mentors including Takao Kagawa, Shozen Kumoi, and Luis Oscar Gómez. He held posts at Kyoto Bunkyo University and Bukkyo University.

Satoshi Kono specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo in 2000 under doctoral supervisor Kiyotaka Kimura and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Kyoto University by ~2012, where he also served as an assistant professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (~2012–2016).

Satya Swarup Misra worked in linguistics and Indology. He held posts as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Lucknow and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

Satya Vrat Shastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Punjabi University and Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1955), and held posts at the University of Delhi (~1955–1995) and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He held posts at the University of Dhaka (1921–1947), University of Calcutta (1947–1956), and Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).
Saudamini Bahulikar specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Harvard University (~1966–1972) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under U Paññāvanta and Mahasi Sayadaw. He served as abbot at Mahāvijjodaya Chaung Monastery, founded Dhammananda Vihara, and became Chancellor of International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (~1998–2005).
Sayaka Sonoda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at Toyo University (~2012–2016) under the doctoral supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.

Scott A. Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union (1998–2008) under Richard K. Payne and became a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies around 2008.
Scott Dalby is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and held a post as a lecturer at Amsterdam University College.

Scott Pacey works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at the Australian National University (~2006–2011) and held posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2011) and the University of Manchester (~2019).
Sean D. Gaffney specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (~1996–2003) under Tadeusz Skorupski and held an academic post there.
See Mui Yian is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong (~2006–2010) under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Seema Alavi works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1987–1991) and held academic posts at the University of Delhi (~2008–2020) and Ashoka University (~2020).
Seigai Omura worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) and served as a professor at Tokyo School of Fine Arts in 1911.
Seiichi Mizuno specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928) and later served there as a professor (~1949–1968).
